# Zoho CRM API: OAuth 2.0 Setup, Tokens and Core Endpoints

By [George Mustoe](/about/) [How we review](/methodology/) Zoho CRMREST APIOAuth 2.0integrationdeveloper

The [Zoho CRM API](/go/zoho/?p=%2Fcrm%2Fdeveloper%2Fdocs%2Fapi%2Fv7%2F) is a [REST](https://restfulapi.net/) interface that lets developers read, write, and synchronize CRM records programmatically using [OAuth 2.0](https://oauth.net/2/) authentication. This integration guide walks through self-client app registration, token flows, the core endpoints you will hit most often, and the patterns that keep production integrations stable across data centers and rate limits. For broader CRM API patterns, see the [Zoho Desk API helpdesk integration guide](/guides/zoho-desk-api-helpdesk-integration-guide/) which uses similar conventions.

## What Does the Zoho CRM API Do?

The Zoho CRM API exposes nearly every object in the CRM - leads, contacts, accounts, deals, tasks, custom modules, layouts, users, and metadata - as REST resources. Developers use it to push form submissions into the lead pipeline, sync deal stages with billing systems, mirror contact data into a data warehouse, or build custom mobile experiences on top of the same data sales reps see in the web UI.

Zoho operates on a regional architecture, which is the single most important fact to internalize before writing any code. Records created in the EU data center are not visible from the US data center, and the API base URL is data-center specific. The standard endpoints are `zohoapis.com` (US), `zohoapis.eu` (EU), `zohoapis.in` (India), `zohoapis.com.au` (Australia), `zohoapis.com.cn` (China), `zohoapis.jp` (Japan), and `zohoapis.ca` (Canada). Calling the wrong region returns an authorization error even when the access token is valid.

The current versioned path is `/crm/v6/` with `/crm/v7/` available for newer endpoints. Always pin to a specific version in production. The platform serves millions of users worldwide across these regions, and the multi-tenant architecture means rate limits apply per organization, not per user.

## What Tools Do You Need for Zoho CRM API Development?

Before writing a single line of integration code, you want a fast feedback loop. Three tools cover the essentials. First, an HTTP client - [Postman](https://www.postman.com/), [Insomnia](https://insomnia.rest/), or [HTTPie](https://httpie.io/) - to exercise endpoints interactively before encoding them. Second, your IDE of choice with a REST client extension if you prefer to keep request collections in version control. Third, a Zoho developer account with API access enabled.

A Zoho developer account is just a regular Zoho account with the API Console activated. Sign in at the [API console](https://api-console.zoho.com/) (swapping the TLD for your data center) using the same credentials you use for the CRM web app. The console is where you will create OAuth clients, view scopes, and generate self-client codes. If you plan to test against real data, create a sandbox or trial workspace separate from your production org. Trying to debug a misbehaving webhook against live customer records is a fast way to corrupt deal stages.

For language SDKs, Zoho publishes [official libraries](/go/zoho/?p=%2Fcrm%2Fdeveloper%2Fdocs%2Fsdk%2F) for Java, Python, Node.js, PHP, C#, and Ruby. They are convenient but optional. Every example in this guide uses raw HTTP so the concepts translate directly to whichever stack you ship. Pair this with the [Zoho CRM workflow automation guide](/guides/zoho-crm-workflow-automation-guide/) when integration triggers business automations.

## What Are the Account, Permission, and Plan Prerequisites?

API access is included from Standard ($14/month annual per user annual) and above; the Free plan has limited or no API access. If you are evaluating Zoho CRM specifically because of the API, start a paid trial rather than the Free tier. The Free plan supports up to 3 users and basic CRUD in the UI, but it does not give developers a stable API surface to build against. For a full breakdown of what each tier unlocks for API work, see the [Zoho CRM pricing page](/go/zoho-crm/?p=%2Fcrm%2Fpricing).

The plan tier also gates certain endpoints. Zia AI features - lead scoring predictions, anomaly detection, sentiment analysis on emails, churn prediction - require the Enterprise plan ($40/month annual per user annual) or Ultimate ($52/month annual per user annual). The [Zoho CRM Zia AI features guide](/guides/zoho-crm-zia-ai-features-guide/) breaks down which Zia outputs are accessible programmatically. Blueprint process automation and advanced workflow rules unlock at Professional ($23/month annual per user annual). If your integration depends on triggering workflows or reading Zia outputs, match the plan to the integration before quoting timelines.

Permissions matter inside the org as well. The CRM user whose credentials authorize the OAuth client must have permission for every module the integration touches. A common gotcha: the integration developer has admin rights, the production service account does not, and the integration silently returns 401 on the Deals module after deploy. Audit the service account profile before going live.

For deeper context on tier differences, see the [Zoho CRM tool page](/tools/zoho-crm/) which breaks down plan-by-plan features.

## Step 1: Register a Self-Client App in Zoho API Console

Most server-to-server integrations use the [Self-Client OAuth flow](/go/zoho/?p=%2Fdeveloper%2Foauth%2Fself-client%2Fauthorization-code-flow.html). There is no redirect URL, no consent screen for end users, just a long-lived refresh token tied to your service account.

Walk through the API Console:

1. Sign in to `api-console.zoho.com` (US) or the regional equivalent for your data center.
2. Click “Add Client” and choose “Self Client”.
3. Confirm the warning - self-client tokens grant the same access as the user creating them.
4. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Store them in a secrets manager, never in source control.
5. Open the “Generate Code” tab. Enter the scopes you need, set a duration (3-10 minutes is enough), and a portal description.

Scope strings follow the pattern `ZohoCRM.MODULE.OPERATION`. For full read/write across the standard modules, request:

`ZohoCRM.modules.ALL ZohoCRM.settings.ALL ZohoCRM.users.READ ZohoCRM.org.READ`

Narrower scopes are better for production. If your integration only updates contacts, request `ZohoCRM.modules.contacts.ALL` and nothing else. The principle of least privilege limits blast radius if the refresh token leaks.

The console returns a grant code. Treat it as single-use - you have minutes to exchange it for an access and refresh token before it expires.

## Step 2: OAuth 2.0 Authentication Flow Explained

Zoho CRM API uses standard [OAuth 2.0](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749) with three client types:

- **Server-based** (web app with backend): full authorization code flow with redirect URL.
- **Self-Client** (server-to-server, no UI): grant code generated in the API Console, exchanged for tokens.
- **Mobile or native**: [PKCE flow](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636) for installed apps.

For most integration work the Self-Client flow is the right choice. The flow has three actors: the resource owner (the Zoho user who clicked “Generate Code”), the client (your integration), and the authorization server (`accounts.zoho.com` or its regional equivalent).

The mental model: the grant code proves a human authorized your client. The refresh token is the durable credential you store. The access token is the short-lived bearer credential you actually attach to API requests. Access tokens expire in one hour. Refresh tokens are long-lived and survive until revoked.

Two endpoints matter:

- Token endpoint: `https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token` (swap `.com` for your data center, e.g. `accounts.zoho.eu`).
- API base: `https://www.zohoapis.com/crm/v6/` (again, regional).

Never hard-code the data center. Build it from a config value so the same code can be deployed against EU, US, and IN tenants without a fork.

## Step 3: Generate and Refresh Access Tokens

Exchange the grant code for tokens with a single POST. Do this once, store the refresh token, and discard the grant code.

`curl -X POST https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token \ -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \ -d "client_id=1000.YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \ -d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -d "code=GRANT_CODE_FROM_CONSOLE"`

The response looks like this:

`{ "access_token": "1000.abc123...", "refresh_token": "1000.def456...", "api_domain": "https://www.zohoapis.com", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600 }`

The `api_domain` field is gold. It tells you exactly which regional base URL to use for subsequent calls, so you do not have to maintain a region lookup table on the client side. Persist `refresh_token` and `api_domain` in your secrets store.

To mint a new access token from the refresh token:

`curl -X POST https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token \ -d "grant_type=refresh_token" \ -d "client_id=1000.YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \ -d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -d "refresh_token=1000.def456..."`

In production, wrap this in a token manager. The pattern: cache the access token in memory or Redis, attach a TTL slightly shorter than `expires_in` (55 minutes is a safe default), and refresh proactively. Do not refresh on every API call - that is what burns through OAuth quota. A simple “is this token within 5 minutes of expiry” check before each call is enough.

If the refresh request returns `INVALID_TOKEN` or `invalid_code`, the refresh token has been revoked. Common causes: an admin re-installed the client, the underlying user lost permission, or someone manually revoked the grant. The integration must surface a re-authorization path for the operations team rather than silently retrying.

## Step 4: Core Zoho CRM API Endpoints

The Zoho CRM API documentation lists hundreds of endpoints, but day-to-day work centers on a handful. Every authenticated request attaches `Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken ACCESS_TOKEN` as a header.

The records endpoint family handles CRUD for any module. The pattern is `/crm/v6/MODULE_API_NAME` where the module name is `Leads`, `Contacts`, `Accounts`, `Deals`, `Tasks`, `Events`, `Calls`, or any custom module API name you defined.

`# Fetch the first page of contacts curl -H "Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken 1000.abc123..." \ "https://www.zohoapis.com/crm/v6/Contacts?fields=First_Name,Last_Name,Email&per_page=200"`

A successful response wraps records in a `data` array with an `info` block for pagination:

`{ "data": [ { "id": "5725767000000123456", "First_Name": "Ada", "Last_Name": "Lovelace", "Email": "ada@example.com", "Modified_Time": "2026-04-30T14:22:11+00:00" } ], "info": { "per_page": 200, "count": 1, "page": 1, "more_records": false } }`

Always pass the `fields` query parameter. Without it, v6 and v7 require it for record queries and will reject the call. Listing exact fields also keeps payloads small and predictable.

To create a record, POST to the same endpoint with a `data` array:

`curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken 1000.abc123..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "data": [ { "First_Name": "Grace", "Last_Name": "Hopper", "Email": "grace@example.com", "Lead_Source": "Web" } ], "trigger": ["workflow"] }' \ "https://www.zohoapis.com/crm/v6/Leads"`

The `trigger` array controls whether assignment rules, workflows, and approval flows fire. Pass an empty array to suppress them during bulk loads.

Other endpoints worth memorizing: `/users` for user lookups (useful for record ownership), `/settings/modules` to discover available modules and custom fields, `/settings/fields` to introspect field metadata for any module, and `/coql` to run [COQL queries](/go/zoho/?p=%2Fcrm%2Fdeveloper%2Fdocs%2Fapi%2Fv6%2FCOQL-Overview.html) (a SQL-like dialect across modules). Bulk Read and Bulk Write APIs handle large data jobs asynchronously and are the right tool for any payload over a few thousand records.

For event-driven integrations, the Notification API (Zoho’s [webhook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webhook) system) lets you subscribe to record events and receive HTTP callbacks. This avoids polling for changes and is the foundation of any near-real-time sync.

## Step 5: Map Data Between Systems (Records, Modules, Layouts)

The hardest part of any CRM integration is rarely the HTTP. It is the data model.

Zoho CRM organizes data into modules. Out of the box you get Leads, Contacts, Accounts, Deals, Tasks, Events, and Calls. Custom modules extend the schema for industry-specific objects (e.g. Properties for real estate, Patients for healthcare). Each module has fields, layouts (which fields appear on which page), and lookup relationships to other modules.

When mapping an external system into Zoho, walk the model in this order:

1. **Identify the canonical Zoho module** for each external entity. A “user” in your SaaS likely maps to a Contact, your “company” to an Account, and your “subscription” to a Deal or a custom module.
2. **Reconcile field types**. Zoho field types include Single Line, Multi Line, Email, Phone, Picklist, Multi-Picklist, Date, DateTime, Currency, Decimal, Lookup, and User. Picklists are particularly tricky - the API accepts only values defined in the picklist. Trying to write an arbitrary string to a picklist field returns `INVALID_DATA`.
3. **Handle lookup fields**. Lookup fields point to a record ID in another module. To set a Contact’s Account, write `"Account_Name": {"id": "5725767000000234567"}`. Trying to write a string here will fail.
4. **Decide on idempotency keys**. Zoho’s `id` is an opaque numeric string. For external sync, use `External_ID` (a built-in reserved field) or a custom field with a unique constraint. The Upsert endpoint (`PUT /crm/v6/MODULE/upsert`) takes a `duplicate_check_fields` array and either inserts or updates based on a match.

`curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken 1000.abc123..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "data": [{"Email": "ada@example.com", "First_Name": "Ada", "Last_Name": "Lovelace"}], "duplicate_check_fields": ["Email"] }' \ "https://www.zohoapis.com/crm/v6/Contacts/upsert"`

Upsert is the workhorse of sync integrations. It removes the “does this record already exist” round trip and lets you ship a one-pass importer.

Layouts add another wrinkle. A field can be required on one layout and hidden on another. The API respects required fields. If your integration writes to a layout that requires `Industry` and you omit it, the call fails. Either include the field or use the `apply_feature_execution` array to bypass layout validation where allowed.

## Step 6: Test Your Integration with Postman

A well-organized [Postman](https://www.postman.com/) collection compresses days of trial-and-error into hours. Build the collection once, share it across the team, and use it for every regression check before deploys.

Set up an environment with these variables:

- `client_id`
- `client_secret`
- `refresh_token`
- `access_token` (populated by a pre-request script)
- `api_domain`
- `account_domain` (e.g. `https://accounts.zoho.com`)

Add a pre-request script to the collection root that mints a fresh access token if the cached one is older than 50 minutes:

`const tokenAgeMs = Date.now() - (pm.environment.get("token_minted_at") || 0); if (tokenAgeMs > 50 * 60 * 1000) { pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.environment.get("account_domain") + "/oauth/v2/token", method: "POST", body: { mode: "urlencoded", urlencoded: [ { key: "grant_type", value: "refresh_token" }, { key: "client_id", value: pm.environment.get("client_id") }, { key: "client_secret", value: pm.environment.get("client_secret") }, { key: "refresh_token", value: pm.environment.get("refresh_token") } ] } }, (err, res) => { const body = res.json(); pm.environment.set("access_token", body.access_token); pm.environment.set("api_domain", body.api_domain); pm.environment.set("token_minted_at", Date.now()); }); }`

Now every request in the collection just attaches the standard `Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken` header with the Postman variable for the access token, and the script handles refresh transparently.

Group requests by module: a “Contacts” folder with Get, List, Create, Update, Upsert, Delete. Save useful sample responses as examples so junior teammates can see the expected payload shape without hitting the live API. When something breaks in production, you have a runnable diagnostic kit ready.

## Common Integration Patterns and Recipes

A few patterns cover most integration shapes:

**Pattern: Form-to-Lead.** A marketing form posts to your backend, your backend creates a Lead in Zoho. Always set `Lead_Source` and any [UTM fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTM_parameters). Trigger workflow on insert so assignment rules fire. The [Zoho CRM setup guide for small business](/guides/zoho-crm-setup-guide-small-business/) covers the lead module configuration to align with this pattern.

**Pattern: Two-way Contact Sync.** Your product database is the source of truth for contact metadata, Zoho is the source of truth for sales notes. Use `Modified_Time` watermarks on both sides. Pull changes since the last watermark, resolve conflicts on a per-field basis. Store a sync state table so you never repeat work after a crash.

**Pattern: Deal Stage Webhook.** Zoho fires a Notification API webhook when a deal moves to “Closed Won”. Your webhook handler validates the signature, looks up the deal, and provisions the customer in your billing system. Always make webhook handlers idempotent - Zoho will retry on 5xx responses.

**Pattern: Bulk Initial Load.** For migrating 100K records, never use the standard records POST. Use the Bulk Write API: upload a CSV to file storage, kick off a bulk job, poll the job status, download the result CSV. The standard API will rate-limit you long before the load completes; bulk endpoints are designed for it.

**Pattern: COQL for Reporting.** When you need to join across modules - “all deals over $50K with their account industry and owner email” - use COQL rather than three separate queries. It keeps the round trips down and lets the database do the join.

For inspiration on which integrations actually drive ROI, the best AI CRM tools 2026 roundup covers comparable platforms, and best Zapier alternatives is useful if you are evaluating no-code middleware as a complement to direct API work.

## How Do You Handle Errors, Rate Limits, and Best Practices?

Production integrations live or die by their error handling. Zoho returns errors with a code, a status, and a human message in the response body. The codes you will see most often:

- `INVALID_DATA`: payload field failed validation. Check field types and required fields.
- `INVALID_TOKEN`: access token expired or revoked. Refresh and retry once.
- `OAUTH_SCOPE_MISMATCH`: token does not have permission for this scope. Re-authorize with broader scopes.
- `MANDATORY_NOT_FOUND`: a layout-required field was omitted.
- `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: rate limit hit. Back off and retry with exponential delay.
- `DUPLICATE_DATA`: unique field violation. Use upsert or look up the existing record.

Rate limits in Zoho CRM apply per organization per day and per concurrent request. The exact numbers vary by plan and change over time, so always reference Zoho’s official API documentation for current values rather than baking limits into code as constants. Treat 429-style responses as a signal to back off, not a permanent failure. A token-bucket rate limiter on the client side prevents your integration from exhausting the org-wide quota and breaking other systems that share the same Zoho tenant.

Best practices that matter in production, several of which echo broader [Google API design guidelines](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apis/design):

1. **Always paginate.** Never assume a list endpoint returns the whole result set. Loop on the `more_records` flag.
2. **Store the `api_domain` returned from the token exchange** and use it as the base URL. Do not parse the user’s email or guess from a config file.
3. **Log the `x-request-id` response header** on every API call. Zoho support uses it to trace issues, and it transforms a vague “the integration is broken” ticket into a five-minute fix.
4. **Validate webhook signatures.** Zoho includes an HMAC signature in Notification API callbacks. Verify it before trusting any payload.
5. **Use sandbox for schema changes.** Custom field additions, picklist value changes, and module renames break integrations. Test against a sandbox first.
6. **Plan for token revocation.** Build a re-authorization flow that an ops user can complete in under five minutes. The fastest integrations to recover from incidents are the ones with a one-click reauth page.

Following these patterns separates integrations that survive a year from integrations that page someone every Monday.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Zoho CRM have an API?

Yes. Zoho CRM exposes a comprehensive REST API covering nearly every object in the CRM - leads, contacts, accounts, deals, tasks, events, custom modules, layouts, users, and metadata. The current versioned path is `/crm/v6/` with `/crm/v7/` available for newer endpoints. Authentication is OAuth 2.0, and SDKs are published for Java, Python, Node.js, PHP, C#, and Ruby.

### How do I authenticate with the Zoho CRM API?

The Zoho CRM API uses OAuth 2.0 with three client types: Server-based (web apps with a redirect URL), Self-Client (server-to-server with no UI), and Mobile or Native (PKCE flow). For most integrations, the Self-Client flow is simplest: register a client in the API Console, generate a grant code, and exchange it for an access token and a long-lived refresh token. Every API request attaches an `Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken TOKEN` header.

### Is Zoho CRM API free?

API access is included from the Standard plan ($14/month annual per user annual) and above. The Free plan, which supports up to 3 users, has limited or no API access and is not recommended for serious integration work. Advanced API features such as Zia AI predictions and sentiment analysis require the Enterprise plan ($40/month annual per user annual) or Ultimate ($52/month annual per user annual). Developers should start with a paid trial rather than the Free plan when evaluating API capabilities.

### What is the Zoho CRM API rate limit?

Zoho CRM enforces rate limits per organization per day and on concurrent requests. The exact numbers vary by plan and change over time, so always reference Zoho’s official API documentation for current limits rather than hard-coding values. When you hit a limit, the API returns a `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error. Production integrations should implement a client-side rate limiter and exponential backoff to stay well within quota.

### How do I refresh an access token in Zoho CRM API?

Access tokens expire after one hour. To refresh, POST to the OAuth token endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`, your client ID, client secret, and the refresh token you stored from the original grant exchange. The response returns a new access token valid for another hour. Refresh tokens are long-lived and only become invalid when revoked, so build a token manager that caches the access token, refreshes it proactively before expiry (around 50 to 55 minutes is safe), and surfaces a re-authorization path if the refresh token is ever rejected.
